purpose: Define the meaning and interpretation limits of every retained value, action, operator and matching pattern without requiring an implementation language.

authority.canonical_business_rules: Domain chapters, mathematical contracts, record definitions and reviewed acceptance outcomes define business obligations. Structural decision trees supplement them with order and branches; they do not automatically resolve every external capability or override.
authority.conflict_handling: Identify the specific conflict and its affected operation. Do not silently discard either a business invariant or a retained branch. Resolve the intended baseline behavior or document an explicitly approved correction before claiming equivalence.
authority.validation_level: This file is a semantic reference catalog, not proof that translated operations have executed, not a universal executable schema, and not certification of full dependency closure.
authority.excluded_scopes: Deployment choices, historical reference behavior and acceptance-support procedures do not become required business services merely because their decision trees exist.

reference_resolution.base_namespace: schemas/operations after the repository directory consolidation; the catalog namespace is the manifest directory, not the directory of an individual partition fragment.
reference_resolution.fragments: A fragment after the number-sign character identifies the named top-level semantic section in this file. It is not a source line and requires no external file.

keys.procedure_semantics: Resolve relative to the operations catalog namespace. The value decision-semantics.json identifies this contract.
keys.semantics: Resolve a catalog-level semantic reference relative to the operations catalog namespace.
keys.interpretation_contract: Resolve the file relative to the operations catalog namespace, then select its named semantic section.
keys.operation_identifier: Look up the exact identifier in operation-index.json and its ordered partitions; resolve the returned contract catalog path from the repository root.
keys.locally_resolved_operations: Resolve each exact operation identifier through operation-index.json. A link identifies a declared body, not permission to bypass dynamic dispatch.
keys.component: Resolve the exact component identifier through its published component context catalog. Load relevant module and behavior context; the identifier is not a filesystem path.
keys.context_bound_capabilities: Names requiring explicit scope, dependency, receiver or adapter resolution. They are not automatically global built-ins.
keys.partitioning.fragments.path: Resolve relative to the catalog manifest directory. Concatenate the declared entry arrays in fragment order; an empty manifest array does not mean an empty catalog.
keys.syntax_and_scope_contract: Resolve relative to the operations catalog namespace and select the named semantic section.
keys.contract.catalog: For an embedded_behavior_contract, resolve the linked catalog from the repository root and select contract.identifier in its entries or partitions.

evaluation_model.order: Evaluate ordinary operands in their declared order, once each, unless the specific short-circuit, deferred, conditional, assignment-target or resource rule says otherwise.
outcomes: continue with a value or next action
evaluation_model.absence: A present absence value is distinct from an unbound name, a missing mapping key, a withheld field and a required parameter omitted by a caller.
evaluation_model.mutation: Local binding, member assignment and indexed assignment modify the current object graph according to its bound object protocol. They do not inherently persist a document, validate financial rules, commit, roll back or emit events.
evaluation_model.object_identity: Mutable values can be shared through several references. Ordinary assignment does not deep-copy them. Fixed-order collections can contain shared mutable members.
evaluation_model.unsupported: An unresolved construct or unbound required capability blocks behavioral completion for that path; never turn it into absence, zero, success or no effect.

truth_and_coercion.true_values: Nonempty primitive collections and text and nonzero primitive numbers are true. The text values zero and false written as nonempty text remain true. Custom records and objects require their bound truth or length protocol.
truth_and_coercion.numeric_strings: The value member of a number node is a textual encoding of a numeric scalar. A text node containing the same characters remains text until an explicitly resolved conversion capability converts it.
truth_and_coercion.implicit_conversion: Do not apply financial helper coercion globally. Generic operations on incompatible kinds fail unless their resolved value protocol defines the operation. The generic numeric helper can map invalid input to zero only when that helper is actually called.
truth_and_coercion.numeric_profile: Integral and fractional arithmetic, nonfinite values, overflow, rounding and representation require the selected numeric profile. Financial acceptance is governed by the documented domain precision and rounding boundaries; the decision tree does not justify globally rounding every value or substituting exact decimal arithmetic without comparing outcomes.
truth_and_coercion.truth_numbers: For ordinary primitive numeric comparison and arithmetic, false and true can participate as zero and one. A strict external data schema can reject such interchange before evaluation. Keep truth_value distinct in the serialized decision structure.
truth_and_coercion.custom_protocols: Custom comparison, iteration, formatting, membership, numeric conversion, indexing and truth behavior are capabilities. Resolve them explicitly; an unknown object is not automatically a plain record mapping.

identifier_literals.canonical_use: Use symbolic_value.value as canonical record, field or option identity only in the identity namespace identified by the consuming operation and identifier_roles.
identifier_literals.text_use: When the same token participates in free text or external interchange, use text_when_not_used_as_identifier when supplied and the published adapter mapping. Canonical field naming is not permission to rename provider payload keys or message content.
identifier_literals.ambiguous_use: A text node with canonical_identifier_candidates requires the actual record or member context before selecting a candidate. Do not choose the first candidate, merge them, or treat candidates as synonyms.
identifier_literals.plain_symbolic_values: When identifier_roles is absent, a symbolic value denotes the retained canonical semantic value, commonly an option or state. Its use still follows the consuming field or service contract.
identifier_literals.namespace_separation: Local variable binding names, public parameter names, record field names and wire field names are different namespaces. Equality of spelling does not prove they identify the same object.
identifier_literals.member_context: A member_value may carry name_when_not_record_member and binding_requirement. Use its canonical name only for a confirmed record/field namespace; for an ordinary external receiver resolve the retained external member name under its capability protocol.
identifier_literals.ambiguous_members: A member_value with canonical_member_candidates requires the confirmed receiver record definition before selecting the canonical field. The context_selected_member marker is unresolved selection metadata, never a real field name or a default candidate.

binding_and_calls.local_binding: Resolve value_reference in the operation local frame, the captured enclosing operation frames, the module context, then explicitly bound shared capabilities as applicable. A local binding can shadow a same-spelled capability or declared helper. Reading a required but uninitialized local raises an unbound-value failure.
binding_and_calls.binding_disambiguation: Suffixes distinguishing colliding neutral names are stable local binding identifiers, not business suffix rules. Use parameter name and binding_name links exactly; do not independently normalize them again.
binding_and_calls.enclosing_bindings: bind_enclosing_values with module scope redirects that name to its module binding; enclosing_operation redirects to an existing captured operation binding. These declarations are lexical scope rules, not ordinary data assignments.
binding_and_calls.class_context: A behavior declaration has its own namespace and inheritance context. An unqualified name inside a method is not automatically a sibling method. Member lookup must use the receiver and the effective override chain.
operation_resolution: Resolve and evaluate the operation value before its arguments.
Evaluate declared positional arguments and collection expansions in order, followed by the named-argument entries and mapping expansions in order.
Select the effective callable, including receiver binding and wrappers. An operation_identifier is a declared-body link subject to resolution_basis and dispatch_requirement.
Bind positional-only, positional-or-named, named-only, remaining positional, and remaining named parameters according to the parameter declarations.

For resolved_callee_parameter, binding_name identifies the exact local parameter. For callee_public_name_requires_context_binding, resolve name in the effective callable public namespace. For expand_mapping_then_bind_at_callee, expand its keys under that namespace.

Reject duplicate assignment of one ordinary parameter, duplicate named keys, missing required parameters, excess positional values without a remaining-positional parameter, and unknown named values without a remaining-named parameter.

A positional-only name supplied as a named key cannot fill that positional parameter. It can be collected as a distinct remaining-named entry when that parameter exists, while the positional requirement still applies.
Apply omitted-parameter defaults; an explicit absence argument is a supplied value and does not trigger the default.
Invoke the effective callable and preserve its returned value, failure, mutation or deferred execution contract.
binding_and_calls.defaults: Evaluate default expressions when the operation value is defined in its declaring context, then retain those default values with that callable. Do not reevaluate them on each invocation. A mutable default may consequently be shared across invocations; replacing it with a fresh collection changes behavior unless explicitly approved.
binding_and_calls.wrappers: Evaluate definition wrapper expressions at definition. Apply wrappers from the last listed wrapper toward the first to the newly defined operation or behavior. Authorization, caching, regional routing and transaction effects supplied by wrappers are dependencies, not optional annotations.
binding_and_calls.shape_declarations: Declared argument or result shapes describe interpretation and validation context. They do not automatically coerce values or instantiate records. Specialized annotation or behavior-construction machinery must be bound if observable.
capability_binding_record: truth, iteration and operator protocols where used
binding_and_calls.unresolved_boundary: A lexically resolved helper link is not proof that module initialization, imported aliases, wrappers, inherited overrides, object protocols or external services have been resolved. Dependent paths remain structurally described until those bindings are supplied.
binding_and_calls.external_parameter_namespace: external_parameter_text preserves the incoming external keyword namespace. The collision-safe name/public_parameter_name and a resolved binding_name identify neutral local parameter bindings. For an external or dynamic callable, bind retained external text through its adapter rather than assuming a caller-local spelling is a callee parameter.
binding_and_calls.captured_values: Captured enclosing bindings remain live references according to their lexical scope. They are not automatically deep-copied snapshots taken at definition; a later change in an enclosing binding can affect a subsequently invoked closure.
binding_and_calls.import_resolution: The resolution basis unconditional_import_or_unambiguous_reexport_subject_to_runtime_binding identifies a statically unambiguous imported or reexported declared body. The actual module initialization, alias binding, wrappers and later rebinding remain required context.

transaction_boundaries.local_assignment: set_values, update_value and remove_values are local/object operations. A record field assignment normally changes the in-memory document; its save/submission/cancellation service determines persistence.
transaction_boundaries.external_calls: An operation_result can call a pure calculation, a query, a document command, a direct storage write, an external delivery or a transaction-control capability. Its name alone cannot classify the effect.
transaction_boundaries.failure_handling: Catching a failure does not automatically roll back storage, undo an external payment, cancel callbacks or reverse previous commits. The invoked capability and enclosing transaction define those effects.
transaction_boundaries.scoped_resources: A scoped resource can be a lock, file, transaction scope, identity override or other capability. Acquisition and cleanup alone do not imply commit or rollback.

absence.interpretation: Produce an explicit absent value. Do not resolve a missing name or failed lookup to this value automatically.

truth_value.interpretation: Produce the encoded true or false value.

number.interpretation: Produce a numeric scalar from its retained numeric text; it is not an ordinary text value.
number.requirements_and_limits: Preserve integer versus fractional interpretation and the bound numeric profile. The textual encoding alone does not authorize a different rounding policy.

complex_number.interpretation: Produce a complex value with the specified real and imaginary numeric components.
complex_number.requirements_and_limits: Ordering and business-money interpretation are not defined for ordinary complex values; resolve the consuming capability.

byte_sequence.interpretation: Produce an ordered sequence of byte values, each from zero through 255. It is distinct from character text.

unspecified_dimension.interpretation: Produce the distinguished unspecified-dimension marker used by a consuming indexing or type protocol. It is not absence or a wildcard match by itself.

text.interpretation: Produce retained character text; a text that looks numeric stays text.
text.requirements_and_limits: Candidate identifiers require consuming-context resolution under identifier_literals.

symbolic_value.interpretation: Resolve a canonical semantic or identifier value according to identifier_literals.
symbolic_value.requirements_and_limits: Do not use a canonical field spelling as an external wire spelling without its adapter contract.

value_reference.interpretation: Read the named bound value using lexical scope. Unbound and explicitly absent values are different outcomes.

member_value.interpretation: Evaluate the owner once, then retrieve its declared member through the bound receiver protocol.
member_value.requirements_and_limits: Member access can calculate, mask, lazily load or raise; it is not automatically a dictionary lookup or database column read. Use retained nonrecord member spelling for external receivers under identifier_literals. Use retained nonrecord member spelling for external receivers under identifier_literals. Use retained nonrecord member spelling for external receivers under identifier_literals.

combine_values.interpretation: Evaluate left then right once each, then apply the selected binary operator and compatible value protocol.

unary_value.interpretation: Evaluate the operand once and apply the selected unary operator.

short_circuit_choice.interpretation: Evaluate operands in order only as needed. first_false_or_last returns the first false-like operand or the final operand; first_true_or_last returns the first true-like operand or the final operand.
short_circuit_choice.requirements_and_limits: Return the actual selected value, not merely its truth. Later operands can have no evaluation or side effects.

ordered_comparison_chain.interpretation: Evaluate initial once, then each right operand only when the preceding comparison permits continuation. The previous right operand becomes the next left operand without reevaluation.
ordered_comparison_chain.requirements_and_limits: Primitive comparisons yield truth values. A custom rich-comparison result can itself require truth evaluation and can be returned unchanged by the final or short-circuited comparison; resolve that protocol.

conditional_value.interpretation: Evaluate when once; evaluate and return only the selected then or otherwise expression.

operation_result.interpretation: Resolve, bind and invoke under binding_and_calls. The result can be immediate, awaitable, iterable, mutating or failing.
operation_result.requirements_and_limits: A linked declared operation body does not bypass wrappers or receiver overrides.

indexed_value.interpretation: Evaluate collection then selection and retrieve the selected member under that collection protocol.
indexed_value.requirements_and_limits: For primitive sequences use zero-based indices and negative offsets from the end; out-of-range index fails. Mapping indices are keys, including negative numeric keys. Missing keys fail unless an explicit provider supplies a default.

interval_selection.interpretation: Construct a slice selector with independently evaluated bounds and step. It does not itself select a collection.
interval_selection.requirements_and_limits: For a primitive sequence, omitted step is one, step zero fails, end is exclusive, negative bounds are relative to length, bounds clamp, and negative step reverses traversal. Omitted end under a negative step differs from an explicit negative-one end.

ordered_collection.interpretation: Evaluate members and expansions in order into a mutable ordered collection. Retain shared object references; do not deep-copy nested values.

fixed_order_collection.interpretation: Evaluate members and expansions in order into a collection with fixed membership. Nested referenced objects can still be mutable.

unique_collection.interpretation: Evaluate members and expansions and retain one value for each primitive equality/hash identity.
unique_collection.requirements_and_limits: Requires admissible hashable keys; display or iteration ordering is not guaranteed by this node. True and numeric one can be equal keys under primitive numeric equality.

keyed_collection.interpretation: Evaluate each entry key then value in order; expand_mapping merges the entry value as a mapping. Later equal keys replace earlier values. Primitive keyed collections retain first-insertion key order; replacing an equal existing key changes its value without moving that key. Mapping expansion follows the supplied mapping iteration order.
keyed_collection.requirements_and_limits: Keys must be admissible under the bound mapping protocol. An absent key with expand_mapping false is an actual absence key; expand_mapping true means expansion, not that key.

collection_projection.interpretation: Apply iteration clauses as nested loops in declared order, binding each target and testing its where_all predicates in order before descending or emitting.
collection_projection.requirements_and_limits: ordered retains every value; unique deduplicates; keyed evaluates each key before value with later equal keys replacing prior values; lazy_ordered defers production. Iteration bindings have a projection-local scope, with captured outer values governed by lexical rules. A keyed projection retains each distinct key at its first insertion position while later equal keys replace its value.

local_mapping_rule.interpretation: Create a callable value capturing its defining scope and evaluated defaults; bind call arguments normally and return the declared value expression when invoked.

composed_text.interpretation: Evaluate and concatenate the already textual or formatted parts in order. Failure in a part stops later evaluation.

formatted_value.interpretation: Evaluate the value, evaluate any dynamic format specification, apply the selected conversion, then the bound formatting protocol.
formatted_value.requirements_and_limits: text is user-oriented text conversion; representation is diagnostic representation; escaped_representation escapes characters outside the basic seven-bit character set in that representation; default invokes formatting directly. Exact quoting, escaping and numeric formatting require a declared profile, not a generic object serialization guess.

expand_collection.interpretation: Expand the referenced iterable into the enclosing collection, argument list or destructuring target.
expand_collection.requirements_and_limits: It is context-sensitive; as a binding target it captures remaining values rather than reading an iterable to emit.

assign_and_use.interpretation: Evaluate value once, assign it to the declared binding target, and return the same value. The target obeys its lexical binding context.

await_completion.interpretation: Evaluate an awaitable value and suspend until its protocol supplies a result or failure.
await_completion.requirements_and_limits: Suspension does not imply background-job creation, parallel execution, transaction commit or durable completion.

emit_value.interpretation: Evaluate and yield the value to the consumer, suspending this operation. On resumption, this expression receives the sent value, or absence for ordinary advancement.
emit_value.requirements_and_limits: Yielding is not returning or posting; generator state and pending cleanup remain live.

emit_each.interpretation: Delegate yield/resumption interaction to the selected iterable or generator, exposing its values in order and preserving delegated completion.
emit_each.requirements_and_limits: The delegated completion value can become the expression result. Sending, throwing and closing require the generator protocol; do not replace delegation with a simple collected list.

relational_selection_template.interpretation: Retain lexical relational clauses and typed tokens for semantic review under relational_selection_templates.
relational_selection_template.requirements_and_limits: Not an executable query or a fully parsed relational tree; caller bindings, nested structure and database semantics remain required.

inferred_from_completion_branches.interpretation: Metadata describing an undeclared result shape. Inspect completion, fall-through, yield and failure branches; this node does not evaluate to a business value.

unresolved_value_construct.interpretation: A value construct is retained but not interpreted. The dependent path cannot be considered complete until its meaning is defined.

configurable_address.interpretation: Produce the retained text only after each address slot has been bound to a real configured address appropriate to its use.
configurable_address.requirements_and_limits: Optional display-only addresses can be deliberately omitted by the experience contract; a live service address requires a resolved and tested external capability. Never invent a host by renaming an application term.

type_union.interpretation: A shape declaration admitting any of the listed alternative shapes.
type_union.requirements_and_limits: This is not integral bit union, an eager conversion, or permission to treat all alternatives as the same record type.

named_shape.interpretation: A named type or value-shape declaration resolved in its type/capability context.
named_shape.requirements_and_limits: Names can denote scalar, collection, record or provider-specific shapes; their descriptive spelling does not implement validation.

absent_value_shape.interpretation: The shape of an explicit absent value. It is metadata admitting absence, not a runtime absent value or an omitted required argument.

unspecified_shape.interpretation: No shape declaration is supplied. This does not mean that every value is business-valid.

forward_declared_shape.interpretation: A retained forward shape reference requiring the applicable declaring type context before resolution.
forward_declared_shape.requirements_and_limits: Do not execute the shape as a business expression or assume its referenced record already exists.

parameterized_shape.interpretation: A shape constructor applied to its ordered type/shape arguments, such as a collection shape with an element shape.
parameterized_shape.requirements_and_limits: Constructor semantics, parameter arity and variance require the resolved type provider; this does not index or construct a business collection.

contextual_shape_expression.interpretation: A shape expression whose interpretation depends on the declaring annotation/type context.
contextual_shape_expression.requirements_and_limits: Its retained value structure is not an instruction to perform business side effects during ordinary data validation.

invalid_address_fixture.interpretation: Retain malformed address text as an inert negative-input fixture. The consuming address validator supplies the declared rejection.
invalid_address_fixture.requirements_and_limits: Do not parse during catalog loading, repair the address, or turn it into a successful empty endpoint; invalid test input is not an instruction to contact a host.

embedded_behavior_contract.interpretation: Retain a link to the exact repository-local neutral behavior identified by contract.catalog and contract.identifier.
embedded_behavior_contract.requirements_and_limits: Resolve catalog from the repository root and identifier within its entries or partitions. The linked behavior is inert until the enclosing capability explicitly requests execution under its scope and restrictions.

embedded_decision_definition.interpretation: Produce inert embedded definition data. A bound evaluation capability chooses ordered-action mode or expression-result mode and grants its environment explicitly.
embedded_decision_definition.requirements_and_limits: Never evaluate decision_steps and expression_result successively for one expression invocation. declared_bindings inventories names; it does not initialize them. incomplete_composed_capability_import is an incomplete excluded compatibility fragment requiring its composition and capability binding before evaluation.

embedded_syntax_fixture.interpretation: Retain a malformed, incomplete, other-grammar or nested-execution fixture without retaining an implementation program.
embedded_syntax_fixture.requirements_and_limits: A required rejection must remain a failure, not an empty successful definition. Failure in the inspected grammar does not establish rejection in another runtime or after valid template composition. A depth-limited fixture remains unresolved until explicitly bound.

add.interpretation: For numbers, arithmetic addition; for compatible text, byte sequences or ordered sequences, concatenation.
add.requirements_and_limits: No implicit conversion of numeric-looking text. A keyed collection does not gain addition merely because it has members. Custom protocols require binding.

subtract.interpretation: For numbers, arithmetic subtraction; for sets under their bound protocol, set difference.
subtract.requirements_and_limits: Other kinds require a compatible declared protocol.

multiply.interpretation: For numbers, arithmetic multiplication. A sequence and an integral repetition count repeat membership in order; a nonpositive count gives an empty sequence.
multiply.requirements_and_limits: Repetition repeats references to mutable elements rather than creating independent copies. Fractional repetition counts fail.

divide.interpretation: Numeric quotient under the selected numeric profile. Zero denominator fails.
divide.requirements_and_limits: A guarded division capability can define zero-on-zero-denominator only when explicitly called.

floor_divide.interpretation: For ordinary real numbers, floor the quotient toward negative infinity. Zero denominator fails.
floor_divide.requirements_and_limits: Negative seven floor-divided by three is negative three, not negative two. Result numeric family and representation follow the bound profile.

remainder_or_text_substitution.interpretation: For ordinary numbers, remainder consistent with floor division and divisor sign. For a text or byte template, perform the template substitution protocol.
remainder_or_text_substitution.requirements_and_limits: For nonzero positive divisor, the ideal remainder lies from zero inclusive to divisor exclusive; negative seven remainder three is two. Floating representation can affect boundary identities. Text substitution must resolve placeholder names, positional values, width, precision, conversion and escaping; it is not arithmetic.

power.interpretation: Exponentiation under the compatible numeric or custom protocol.
power.requirements_and_limits: Negative powers, zero to negative power, fractional powers and complex results require the selected profile; do not impose financial rounding here.

shift_bits_left.interpretation: Shift integral bits left by a nonnegative integral count.
shift_bits_left.requirements_and_limits: Reject a negative count; width and overflow follow the bound integral profile.

shift_bits_right.interpretation: Arithmetic right shift of an ordinary signed integral value by a nonnegative integral count.
shift_bits_right.requirements_and_limits: For unbounded signed integral behavior this agrees with floor division by the corresponding power of two; fixed-width providers must declare their rule.

bit_union.interpretation: Integral bit union; for sets, union; for compatible keyed collections, merge with right-side values replacing equal left keys.
bit_union.requirements_and_limits: For type-shape values this can denote a union shape instead of business arithmetic. Resolve the operand kind. A primitive mapping union retains left key order, replaces matching values in place, and appends newly introduced right keys in right iteration order.

bit_exclusive_union.interpretation: Integral exclusive bit union or set symmetric difference under the compatible protocol.

bit_intersection.interpretation: Integral bit intersection or set intersection under the compatible protocol.

matrix_multiply.interpretation: Matrix multiplication under an explicitly bound dimensional numeric provider.
matrix_multiply.requirements_and_limits: The generic decision contract supplies no default matrix shape, broadcasting or storage implementation.

negate_truth.interpretation: Apply the truth decision and return its opposite as a truth value.

negate_number.interpretation: Apply numeric sign negation or the bound custom unary protocol.

affirm_number.interpretation: Apply unary numeric affirmation; do not interpret numeric-looking text as a number implicitly.

invert_bits.interpretation: Invert integral bits. For unbounded signed integral behavior the result is negative operand minus one. Other providers require an explicit rule.

equal.interpretation: Primitive value equality. Numeric-looking text is not a number; compatible sequences compare their elements and sequence kinds; mappings compare key/value membership; sets compare membership.
equal.requirements_and_limits: Custom equality and nonfinite numeric behavior require the value protocol. Primitive true and one can compare equal.

not_equal.interpretation: Primitive inequality, with any custom inequality operation explicitly resolved.

less_than.interpretation: Strict order for compatible numbers or lexicographically ordered compatible primitive sequences/text; strict subset for sets.
less_than.requirements_and_limits: Incompatible kinds, ordinary mappings and complex values have no generic total order.

less_than_or_equal.interpretation: Nonstrict compatible order or set subset, under the bound value protocol.

greater_than.interpretation: Strict reverse compatible order or strict set superset.

greater_than_or_equal.interpretation: Nonstrict reverse compatible order or set superset.

same_identity.interpretation: Whether both references designate the same runtime object or distinguished singleton.
same_identity.requirements_and_limits: Not business-record-key equality. Two loaded representations of one record can have equal keys and different object identities.

different_identity.interpretation: Whether the runtime object identities differ; it is not ordinary value inequality.

contained_in.interpretation: Membership of the left value in the right container: mapping keys, sequence/set members, or a text substring as applicable.
contained_in.requirements_and_limits: The container membership or iteration protocol can be custom and can fail; it is not automatically a database query.

not_contained_in.interpretation: Negate the membership decision after applying the same right-container membership protocol.

declare_value_shape.interpretation: Record a type or shape declaration without assigning a business value.
declare_value_shape.requirements_and_limits: Do not create an initialized value from shape metadata alone; definition-time annotation machinery is a separate capability.

set_values.interpretation: Evaluate value once, then assign to each target in declared order. Destructuring binds corresponding members and an expanded remainder where declared.
set_values.requirements_and_limits: For a member/index target evaluate its receiver and selector when that target is assigned. Preserve aliasing. An assignment failure need not undo earlier local assignments.

update_value.interpretation: Resolve the target location and read its current value once, evaluate the right value, invoke its in-place operation when supported or the compatible binary operation otherwise, and assign the resulting value back.
update_value.requirements_and_limits: Do not duplicate target evaluation by expanding it into two textual expressions. An in-place mutation can be visible through aliases even if a subsequent target write fails.

complete_with_value.interpretation: Evaluate the value and request completion of the current operation, after required cleanup.
complete_with_value.requirements_and_limits: For a generator, completion terminates iteration and can convey its final result according to that generator protocol.

evaluate.interpretation: Evaluate for its returned value or effects and discard the ordinary result. Failures and suspensions still propagate.

choose_branch.interpretation: Evaluate the condition once, execute only the selected action list, then continue with the enclosing list unless an abrupt outcome propagates.

for_each.interpretation: Evaluate over once, obtain its iterator, bind each yielded member and execute steps. A next-iteration outcome requests the next member.
for_each.requirements_and_limits: Execute after_natural_completion only on normal exhaustion, including an initially empty iterable; not after stop_iteration, operation completion or failure. Asynchronous iteration awaits its iterator protocol.

repeat_while.interpretation: Reevaluate when before each iteration and execute steps while true-like.
repeat_while.requirements_and_limits: Execute after_natural_completion when the test naturally becomes false, including initially false; not after stop_iteration, return or failure.

handle_failures.interpretation: Execute protected steps, select applicable failure handlers in order, run after_success only on normal fall-through with no protected failure, and run always on every exit.
handle_failures.requirements_and_limits: Failure taxonomy, group selection, cleanup priority and temporary failure bindings are defined in failure_and_cleanup. Failure handling alone does not roll back business transactions.

use_scoped_resources.interpretation: Acquire resources in order, enter each scope, bind entry results when requested, execute the body, and exit successfully entered scopes in reverse order.
use_scoped_resources.requirements_and_limits: Later acquisition or entry failure still cleans up prior entered scopes. Exit can suppress a failure or replace an outcome according to its bound protocol; asynchronous resources await entry and exit.

fail.interpretation: Raise the evaluated failure or re-propagate the active failure when propagate_active_failure is true.
fail.requirements_and_limits: An explicit absent cause suppresses displayed causal chaining; an omitted cause retains implicit active context. cause_present distinguishes them. An invalid absence failure does not mean successful completion.

require_condition.interpretation: Evaluate condition; if false-like, evaluate the failure description and raise the applicable assertion failure.
require_condition.requirements_and_limits: acceptance_assertion describes a check in an acceptance-support procedure. runtime_assertion is retained control behavior; execution environments that disable such checks must declare that policy. Assertions are not a substitute for public business validation.

remove_values.interpretation: Remove bindings or selected object members in target order using their deletion protocols.
remove_values.requirements_and_limits: It does not mean delete business document. Missing bindings or keys can fail; indexed collection deletion can shift later positions.

stop_iteration.interpretation: Stop the nearest active loop and skip its after_natural_completion list; execute any intervening cleanup. An enclosing loop continues under its own rules.

next_iteration.interpretation: Advance the nearest active loop after required cleanup. Do not execute later actions in the current iteration.

bind_enclosing_values.interpretation: Declare module or captured enclosing-operation binding scope for those names. It is a lexical resolution rule, not a runtime business mutation.

bind_capability_dependencies.interpretation: Bind named external or shared capabilities to their declared local names from the applicable component context.
bind_capability_dependencies.requirements_and_limits: Dependency loading, initialization, wildcard expansion, aliases and public parameter namespaces require provider resolution; this action does not implement the provider.

define_local_operation.interpretation: Create an operation value in the current scope, capturing enclosing bindings and evaluating defaults and definition wrappers at creation.
define_local_operation.requirements_and_limits: Body executes on invocation or generator advancement, not merely because the definition was encountered. Apply wrappers in reverse listed application order.

define_record_behavior.interpretation: Construct a behavior namespace from the declared inherited providers, execute declarations in that context, apply applicable construction options and wrappers, and bind the resulting behavior value.
define_record_behavior.requirements_and_limits: Inheritance resolution, descriptor lookup and custom construction are capability contracts. A behavior definition is not insertion of a business record.

select_matching_pattern.interpretation: Evaluate subject once, try alternatives in order, and execute the first matching pattern with a true-like applicable guard.
select_matching_pattern.requirements_and_limits: Use guard_present to distinguish no guard from an explicit absent-value guard. Match bindings, failure side effects and pattern protocols are defined in pattern_semantics.

declare_type_alias.interpretation: Declare a named type or shape alias, not a persisted business value.
declare_type_alias.requirements_and_limits: Type parameters or deferred annotation evaluation require the type capability context where observably used.

unresolved_statement.interpretation: Retain an unsupported action for review. Its dependent path cannot be treated as implemented or as no effect.

failure_and_cleanup.handler_selection: For ordinary failures, evaluate applicable categories and select the first matching handler according to the bound failure taxonomy. category_present false is a catch-all handler; an explicit absence category is not a valid catch-all. Bind the active failure for its handler when requested.
failure_and_cleanup.handler_binding_lifetime: The handler failure binding is temporary and is cleared after the handler, including abrupt exit. Do not assume a prior same-spelled local value is restored.
failure_and_cleanup.success_branch: after_success runs only after protected steps finish normally without taking a handler, returning, breaking or continuing. Failures raised in after_success are not caught by those same handlers.
failure_and_cleanup.always_branch: always runs after protected steps, a handler or after_success, including pending return, iteration control and failure. Normal cleanup preserves the pending outcome; a new cleanup failure or explicit cleanup completion replaces it according to the control protocol.
failure_and_cleanup.failure_groups: When handles_failure_group is true, match each handler to the applicable subgroup of failures. Several handlers can run for disjoint subgroups; remaining and newly raised failures propagate as a group. This is not the first-match whole-group rule. Requires an explicitly bound group-failure taxonomy.
failure_and_cleanup.resource_suppression: A scope exit receives the pending failure context. A truth-like suppression result can suppress that failure; normal-return cleanup does not suppress an unrelated pending return. Exit behavior can itself fail and must follow nested cleanup order.
failure_and_cleanup.missing_presence_flags: If legacy translated entries omit category_present, cause_present or guard_present and encode absence, the omitted-versus-explicit distinction may be lost. Treat any behavior-dependent ambiguity as unresolved; do not silently invent catch-all, no-guard or chaining behavior.
failure_and_cleanup.business_effects: These control rules concern evaluation flow. Storage rollback, attachment cleanup, queue callbacks and external reversals require their own explicitly invoked or enclosing transaction contracts.

any_value.interpretation: Match any subject without imposing a value constraint.

equal_value.interpretation: Evaluate the pattern value and test matching equality with the subject under the applicable value protocol.

singleton.interpretation: Match the distinguished absence, true or false singleton by its singleton identity.
singleton.requirements_and_limits: A true singleton pattern must not match numeric one merely because numeric equality can compare them equal.

ordered_sequence.interpretation: Match an admissible sequence by element patterns. Without a remaining-sequence pattern require exact length; with one, match fixed prefix/suffix and capture the intervening ordered values.
ordered_sequence.requirements_and_limits: Ordinary text and byte sequences do not participate as generic sequence patterns. Sequence matching eligibility is a type protocol.

mapping.interpretation: Match required keys and their value patterns against a mapping; extra keys are allowed. Bind a new mapping of unmatched entries when bind_remainder is present.
mapping.requirements_and_limits: Missing required keys cause no match. Key lookup and equality require the mapping protocol and must not become an unrestricted record read.

record_shape.interpretation: Require an instance compatible with the selected behavior/type, then match declared positional and named members.
record_shape.requirements_and_limits: Positional-to-member correspondence comes from that type matching protocol. Member access can have effects; missing members can fail the match while other access failures can propagate.

remaining_sequence.interpretation: Within a sequence pattern, match remaining members and bind them as an ordered collection if requested; absent bind discards them.

bind_matching_value.interpretation: Match its subpattern and, on match, bind the subject to the declared name when present. A nested any_value represents an unconditional capture or discard.

first_matching_alternative.interpretation: Try alternatives in order and use the first matching one.
first_matching_alternative.requirements_and_limits: Alternative capture sets must be compatible. Pattern matching does not guarantee absence of side effects from earlier failed alternatives.

unresolved_pattern.interpretation: Retain an unsupported pattern for review and block claims of complete dependent behavior.

pattern_semantics.subject: Evaluate the subject once for the entire select_matching_pattern action.
pattern_semantics.guard: After a pattern matches and its captures are available, evaluate its guard only when guard_present is true. An absent-value guard is false-like; no guard admits the pattern unconditionally. If the guard is false, continue to the next alternative.
pattern_semantics.binding_scope: Successful captures bind in the enclosing operation scope, not a fresh block-only scope. Guard-false attempts may leave their successful captures visible; partial bindings on a failed pattern are not a portable guaranteed state. Do not depend on their rollback or survival without an explicit fixture.
pattern_semantics.first_success: Only one alternative body executes. If none matches or passes its guard, continue after the selection without executing a body.
pattern_semantics.effects: Custom equality, mapping lookup, attribute access and type matching can evaluate capabilities. A failed match is not proof that no such capability ran.

iteration_and_suspension.sequence_iteration: Read the selected iterator protocol. Mutating a collection during iteration can change later results or fail; do not implicitly snapshot every iterable.
iteration_and_suspension.projection_scope: Projection loop targets have their own scope and do not overwrite ordinary outer loop variables. Captured outer values remain references; assign_and_use follows its specified lexical target and must not be blindly re-scoped.
iteration_and_suspension.lazy_projection: Create the outermost iterator in the defining context when the lazy projection is constructed; defer later iteration, filters and output computation until consumption. Inner iterables are evaluated when their enclosing clause reaches them.
iteration_and_suspension.generating_operations: An operation containing its own emit_value or emit_each constructs is a generating operation. Merely creating the generator does not execute its body. Do not infer generator status from emits inside a separate nested operation.
iteration_and_suspension.asynchronous_operations: An asynchronous operation returns a deferred operation value according to its asynchronous protocol. Awaiting can resume, fail or cancel it; it is not automatically a durable background job.
iteration_and_suspension.cleanup: Completion, failure, cancellation or explicit closing of a suspended operation must honor active resource and cleanup scopes. Abandoning a generator is not a portable immediate-cleanup guarantee.
iteration_and_suspension.ordering: Asynchronous iteration remains ordered by the iterator and action clauses unless an invoked capability explicitly introduces concurrency.

relational_selection_templates.status: A lexical clause-and-token template used to retain query intent. It is not a complete parsed query, prepared statement, or executable relational algebra.

token_roles.text: A retained quoted token. quotation records single versus double quotation; preserve its doubled or backslash escape fragments until the selected dialect interprets them. Double quotation can denote a value or an identifier depending on that dialect.
token_roles.record_or_field: A normalized quoted identifier candidate. Resolve it against canonical record and field definitions, aliases, and dynamic effective metadata; do not assume it is already a valid physical storage name.
token_roles.bound_parameter: A named bound-value placeholder. external_parameter_text retains its external parameter spelling; resolve the canonical placeholder through the caller mapping and consuming context.
token_roles.number: A textual encoding of a query numeric literal under the relational provider numeric rules.
token_roles.term: A normalized unquoted token that can denote an identifier, alias, function, keyword, direction, type or other grammatical term. Determine its role through a full query contract.
token_roles.symbol: A retained punctuation or operator token. Its role depends on surrounding query grammar.
token_roles.positional_parameter: Zero-based ordinal of a positional bound-value placeholder within this template. Bind it to the corresponding supplied query value; do not infer ordinal from surrounding numeric literals.
token_roles.format_parameter: A textual-format placeholder retained separately from bound query values. Resolve its formatting operation and grammar effect independently; it is not automatically a safe bound-value placeholder.
token_roles.qualifier: Identifier qualifier retained separately from the final canonical member, commonly a relation or alias. Resolve its scope before choosing the record/field identity.
token_roles.quotation: Single or double quotation metadata for a text token. Apply the selected dialect once; do not decode retained escaping twice.
token_roles.canonical_member_candidates: Possible canonical identities of a member token. Resolve relation/alias context; no candidate is a permitted default.
token_roles.name_when_not_record_member: Alternate member interpretation when the token is not a canonical business-record field; requires the consuming grammatical or capability context.
token_roles.external_parameter_text: Retained named-placeholder spelling for matching the original caller parameter namespace; canonical field naming alone does not change this binding.

clause_roles.select: Projection expressions and selected fields; duplicates and aggregates must be specified.
clause_roles.join: Join relation; join kind and condition must be recovered from the complete contract.
clause_roles.left_join: Preserve unmatched left rows with absent right values under the relational rules.
clause_roles.right_join: Preserve unmatched right rows with absent left values under the relational rules.
clause_roles.inner_join: Retain matching combinations according to the join predicate.
clause_roles.cross_join: All combinations of the selected relations.
clause_roles.on: Join predicate; moving it to where can change outer-join behavior.
clause_roles.group_by: Grouping keys; aggregate measures require their own calculation and null rules.
clause_roles.having: Predicate applied to grouped or aggregated results.
clause_roles.order_by: Ordered sort expressions, direction, null positioning and tie behavior.
clause_roles.offset: Result starting displacement under the query ordering.
clause_roles.union: Combine compatible result relations with duplicate removal according to the provider.
clause_roles.update: Mutation target; requires explicit update service and authority.
clause_roles.set: Field assignments for a mutation, not an automatic local set_values action.
clause_roles.delete: Deletion relation and predicate; not equivalent to validated business-document cancellation.
clause_roles.insert_into: Insertion destination and optional destination columns.
clause_roles.with: Named subqueries or common relations with nested dependency context.
clause_roles.for_update: Requested locking read within its surrounding transaction.
clause_roles.prefix: Unclassified leading material. It must be interpreted or rejected before execution.

interpretation_requirements: Quoted values are tokenized before clause and comment recognition, preserving quoted clause keywords and comment-like text. Recover nested query boundaries, dialect-specific quotations, aliases and multiword constructs through the complete relational contract; the template remains lexical rather than a parsed grammar.
Bind every placeholder by parameter identity or position; never interpolate untrusted text as query grammar.
Resolve canonical relation and field identities and any dynamic table or column additions.
Define joins, null-aware three-valued predicates, collations, numeric aggregation, date interpretation, ordering, duplicates, limits and lock scope.
Distinguish report/query filtering from permission-aware record access; direct storage capability use does not automatically inherit record permissions.
For mutations, identify transaction ownership and whether domain lifecycle and accounting rules are invoked or intentionally bypassed by a trusted service.

If interpretation of quoting, escaping, qualification, nested structure or placeholder format remains ambiguous, use the reviewed domain/service contract to define the missing behavior and retain the remaining issue explicitly.
relational_selection_templates.prohibition: Do not concatenate these normalized tokens into executable statements or claim that token coverage proves full query semantics.

acceptance_cases.name: numeric text remains text
acceptance_cases.expected: Numeric add gives five; text add gives the two-character text 23; mixed add fails without an explicit compatible conversion.

acceptance_cases.name: short circuit preserves chosen value
acceptance_cases.expected: first_false_or_last returns numeric zero and does not evaluate the second operand.

acceptance_cases.name: floor and remainder for negative dividend
comparison evaluates middle once
acceptance_cases.expected: The condition first less than middle less than last is true and invokes the middle-producing operation once.

acceptance_cases.name: empty iteration natural completion
acceptance_cases.expected: No loop body runs; after_natural_completion runs once.

acceptance_cases.name: break suppresses natural completion
acceptance_cases.expected: The second member is not visited and after_natural_completion does not run.

acceptance_cases.name: explicit absence differs from default
acceptance_cases.expected: The bound argument is absent, not five. Omission, rather than explicit absence, selects the retained default.

acceptance_cases.name: mapping merge and argument expansion differ
acceptance_cases.expected: A keyed_collection merge retains quantity two; passing duplicate named quantity arguments fails binding.

acceptance_cases.name: pattern singleton is identity based
acceptance_cases.expected: The true singleton pattern does not match numeric one even though primitive numeric equality can compare them equal.

acceptance_cases.name: cleanup preserves or replaces pending outcome
acceptance_cases.expected: Normal always cleanup preserves result seven; a new cleanup failure propagates instead of that result.

acceptance_cases.name: assignment does not post
acceptance_cases.expected: The local assignment alone does not establish a submitted business transaction, valid workflow, or ledger posting.

acceptance_cases.name: embedded definition remains inert
acceptance_cases.expected: Loading or storing the definition invokes no capability and writes no business record.

acceptance_cases.name: embedded expression evaluates once
acceptance_cases.expected: Evaluate expression_result once; do not execute the duplicate statement representation first.

acceptance_cases.name: negative fixture is not success
acceptance_cases.expected: Preserve the declared inspected-grammar rejection; do not infer another grammar rejects or replace the fixture with a valid empty definition.

failure_description.value: Stock units per commercial unit must be positive

worked_example.persistence_effect: none; this example computes a quantity and does not save or submit a document

configurable_addresses.slot_binding: Bind every address_slots name once for the evaluated template to an appropriate configured electronic mail address or resource address according to address_kind.
configurable_addresses.purpose: The template retains surrounding content while making deployment-owned help, support, presentation and external service addresses explicit configuration dependencies.
configurable_addresses.live_services: An address used by an actual integration is part of its external capability contract, including destination ownership, operation, authentication, expected result and failure behavior. The slot alone does not define that integration.
configurable_addresses.display_only: A deliberately optional display address can be omitted only when its experience contract permits omission. Do not erase a required service target to make an unresolved operation appear complete.
configurable_addresses.substitution: Resolve only the declared slots as address substitutions before any separately specified text formatting that consumes the result. Preserve other literal text and placeholder syntax; do not interpret the entire template as executable expressions.
configurable_addresses.failure: An unbound required address slot is an unresolved configuration dependency, not a successful empty address or fabricated renamed hostname.

first_false_or_last.interpretation: Return the first evaluated false-like operand; if none is false-like before the end, return the last operand. Do not evaluate remaining operands after selecting one.

first_true_or_last.interpretation: Return the first evaluated true-like operand; if none is true-like before the end, return the last operand. Do not evaluate remaining operands after selecting one.

embedded_decision_definitions.inert_data: Reading, copying or saving an embedded definition does not execute its body or acquire any capability.
embedded_decision_definitions.consumer_selection: The enclosing evaluator explicitly selects statement mode using decision_steps, or expression mode using expression_result. Evaluate the selected representation once; do not run both. The evaluator defines the returned value or output namespace.
embedded_decision_definitions.scope: isolated_literal_execution_scope has its own neutral name bindings. The consumer can explicitly grant outside values, records and capabilities. Do not implicitly import unrestricted caller locals, administrative authority or transaction control.
embedded_decision_definitions.bindings: declared_bindings is a name inventory, not an assignment of default values. Resolve its local definitions and explicitly granted outside values under ordinary lexical rules. context_bound_capabilities still requires resolution and is not a permission grant.
embedded_decision_definitions.composition: incomplete_composed_capability_import cannot execute alone. The enclosing composition contract must supply its missing capability member; excluded_implementation_compatibility does not create a required business feature.
embedded_decision_definitions.failures: Syntax acceptance, access permission, business validation and transaction success are separate outcomes. Catching an embedded failure does not inherently roll back storage.
embedded_decision_definitions.limitations: The neutral representation does not preserve original program spelling, source locations or exact syntax diagnostic text. Byte-level compatibility dependent on those details requires an explicit separate contract.

invalid_address_fixtures.interpretation: Retain malformed text and its expected validation failure without performing address parsing during catalog loading. The actual consumer determines whether and when it rejects; never fabricate a valid destination.
